BREAKING: US housing starts fell -5.2% MoM in September, to an annualized rate of 1.22 million, the # reading since May 2020.

This follows MoM declines of -4.9% and -5.9% in July and August.

Single-family housing starts dropped -4.6% MoM last month, to 859,000, the # since April 2023.

At the same time, multifamily housing starts fell -7.2%, to 349,000, the # since May 2025.

Higher mortgage rates and worsening affordability are heavily weighing on housing demand.

Furthermore, elevated housing inventories and falling homebuilder confidence are discouraging new construction.

The US housing market is frozen.

BREAKING: The 15 largest S&P 500 stocks now account for a record 46.7% of the index’s market value.

By comparison, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, the 15 largest stocks accounted for 27.2% of the S&P 500.

The remaining 485 stocks represent just 53.3%  of the S&P 500’s market cap.

This comes as Nvidia, $NVDA, Apple, $AAPL, Alphabet, $GOOGL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, account for 7.5%, 7.1%, 5.9%, and 5.6%, respectively, or 26.1% combined.

This means just 4 stocks account for more than the next 11 combined.

Furthermore, the combined market cap of the 5 largest stocks now equals that of the bottom 434 stocks in the index, the largest gap on record.

Market concentration is at historic extremes.
